items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: I was talking about Charlie Rosenthal over in Orange, Texas, who was a good friend of Frank Pannier.

ctx.x: Right, yeah, January the 10th, 1996, Real Number 3 with Tech Stevens.

And, you know, as we were saying, Ted, we were talking about writing columns and so forth, about knowing people, about getting involved, having the right kind of connection, so that you could get into the structure of putting something together to inform in a newspaper, because a lot of people call newspaper an organ. items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: I had a meeting with Frank Pena and Rosenthal from out of Port Arthur, Texas.

ctx.x: Did he treat a lot of people like that? Was he very generous?

Well, he was generous to a lot of people. Frank was a likable individual who just cared for people, and he just liked to get involved. And I was thinking about, I had a meeting with Frank Pena and Rosenthal from out of Port Arthur, Texas. I'm trying to think of Rosenthal. He had a theater and a nightclub, and he used to come here and talk to Frank Pena all the time. Sometimes Frank would send some of his talent over there to Orange, Texas, rather. Charlie Rosenthal was his name. Very nice man. I hope he's still…

Oh, definitely. One point. Earl King told me, he said one of the, the most successful, the recent success of the dew drop wasn't, and the attraction wasn't just the music. He said, but he said a lot, the transvestites and the gay reviews.
